---
title: "Plot MSE Multiple Lines"
author: "Santiago Morante"
date: "03/19/2015"
output:
  html_document:
    keep_md: yes
---

This file is intended to plot the Mean Square Error generated during a experiment (frame by frame). It is expected that you have 3 files for different alpha and beta parameters.

To correctly see the plot, first set the working directory (change the next path to the one you want).

```{r}
setwd("../results")
```

Next, introduce the name of the files containing the MSE of your training experiment.

```{r}
filename_training_1 = "motion_results_26.Apr.2015_01:09:03.csv"
alpha_1 = 0.05
lambda_1 = 0.5
filename_training_2 = "motion_results_26.Apr.2015_01:25:33.csv"
alpha_2 = 0.5
lambda_2 = 0.5
filename_training_3 = "motion_results_26.Apr.2015_01:37:20.csv"
alpha_3 = 0.005
lambda_3 = 0.5
filename_training_4 = "motion_results_26.Apr.2015_01:50:16.csv"
alpha_4 = 0.05
lambda_4 = 5
filename_training_5 = "motion_results_26.Apr.2015_02:02:12.csv"
alpha_5 = 0.05
lambda_5 = 0.05

```

Now we define the types of lines and their colors. Also we define other parameters of the plot.

```{r}

# line type: http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Shapes_and_line_types/
type_line_1=3
type_line_2=2
type_line_3=1
type_line_4=4
type_line_5=6


# line colors: http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~tzheng/files/Rcolor.pdf
color_line_1= 'dodgerblue4'
color_line_2= 'black'
color_line_3= 'darkgoldenrod1'
color_line_4= 'firebrick3'
color_line_5= 'forestgreen'

# line width
width = 3

# rectangle transparency
alpha_channel=0.3

```


That's all you need to you. If everything went ok, next chunk should show you the plot.

```{r}
data_training_1 = read.csv(filename_training_1, header = TRUE)
data_training_2 = read.csv(filename_training_2, header = TRUE)
data_training_3 = read.csv(filename_training_3, header = TRUE)
data_training_4 = read.csv(filename_training_4, header = TRUE)
data_training_5 = read.csv(filename_training_5, header = TRUE)


# same for the 3 experiments (theoretically)
x_total = 1:nrow(data_training_1)


# change and final
change = 200
final = nrow(data_training_1)

# different for each of the experiments
y_total_1 = as.numeric(data_training_1$Mean.Square.Error)
y_total_2 = as.numeric(data_training_2$Mean.Square.Error)
y_total_3 = as.numeric(data_training_3$Mean.Square.Error)
y_total_4 = as.numeric(data_training_4$Mean.Square.Error)
y_total_5 = as.numeric(data_training_5$Mean.Square.Error)


############# PLOT #########

par(mar=c(4, 4.2, 1.5, 0.1))
# declare device
plot(0,0,
     xaxs="i",yaxs="i", # to set axis to zero
     xlim = c(0,final),
     ylim = c(0,1),
     type = "n",
     xlab = "Frame", ylab = "Error", main = "Mean Square Error")

############# plot rectangles
rect(0, 0, change, 1,
     border = FALSE, 
     col=rgb(1, 0, 0, alpha=alpha_channel))

rect(change, 0, final,1, 
     border = FALSE, 
     col=rgb(0, 0, 1, alpha=alpha_channel))

############# plot text
text(c(change/2, (final+change)/2 ),
     c(0.5,0.5),
     labels=c("Training","Test"),
     font=2,
     cex=2,
     family="B",
     col = c("white", "white"))

############# plot lines
lines(x_total, y_total_1, 
     type = "l", 
     col = color_line_1, 
     lty = type_line_1, 
     lwd=width)

lines(x_total, y_total_2, 
     type = "l", 
     col = color_line_2,
     lty = type_line_2,
     lwd=width)

lines(x_total, y_total_3, 
     type = "l", 
     col = color_line_3,
     lty = type_line_3,
     lwd=width)

lines(x_total, y_total_4, 
     type = "l", 
     col = color_line_4,
     lty = type_line_4,
     lwd=width)

lines(x_total, y_total_5, 
     type = "l", 
     col = color_line_5,
     lty = type_line_5,
     lwd=width)


############# plot legend

legend('topright',
       legend = c(
           paste("α=", bquote(.(alpha_1)), ", λ=", bquote(.(lambda_1))), 
           paste("α=", bquote(.(alpha_2)), ", λ=", bquote(.(lambda_2))), 
           paste("α=", bquote(.(alpha_3)), ", λ=", bquote(.(lambda_3))),
           paste("α=", bquote(.(alpha_4)), ", λ=", bquote(.(lambda_4))),
           paste("α=", bquote(.(alpha_5)), ", λ=", bquote(.(lambda_5))) ),  
       col=c(color_line_1, color_line_2, color_line_3, color_line_4, color_line_5),
       lty=c(type_line_1, type_line_2, type_line_3, type_line_4, type_line_5),
       lwd=3,
       bty='o', # alternative n /o
       cex=0.75,
       text.width=90) #size of legend

```
